transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I came in because I blew up at one of the younger volunteers over a crooked tablecloth. I don’t usually speak to people that way, and it bothered me afterward.
Has anything particularly stressful or upsetting happened in your life recently?
Well, I got unusually angry with one of the younger volunteers over a crooked tablecloth. I snapped at them, and that’s not how I normally treat people.
Before this happened, had there been a recent major stress or change in your life?
Yes. About a week ago, there was a robbery outside the bank, and things have been off for me since then.
Since the robbery, have unwanted memories of it been popping into your mind?
Yes. Out of nowhere, I’ll hear that man’s rough voice in my head, or see the donation envelope hitting the ground. It happens even when I’m just sitting at my kitchen table.
Since the robbery, have you been avoiding reminders of what happened?
Yes. I’ve been taking the long way around so I don’t have to pass the bank. And I haven’t gone into the festival storage room either—it just brings the whole thing too close.
How long ago did the robbery happen?
About a week ago—ever since the robbery outside the bank.
Since the robbery, have you been feeling jumpy or easily startled?
Yes. A car backfired near the senior center, and I jumped so hard my chest hurt. My hands were shaking for a few minutes afterward.
Did these symptoms start right after the robbery?
Yes, pretty much right afterward. It’s been going on about a week now, since the robbery outside the bank.
During the robbery, did you feel that your life or someone else’s life was in danger?
I’m not sure. It all happened so fast—I just remember being very scared.
Since the robbery, have there been times when you felt detached from yourself or like what was happening around you wasn’t quite real?
I don’t think so. I’ve been upset, but I haven’t noticed feeling detached from myself or like things weren’t real.
Since the robbery, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day?
I’m not sure I’d say depressed most of the day. I’ve been upset about it, but not really down all day.
During the robbery, did it seem like someone might be killed or seriously hurt?
I can’t really say. It was frightening, but I don’t remember thinking someone was going to be killed or seriously hurt.
Did the robber have a weapon?
I remember seeing a gun, yes. But after that, the part where I got knocked down is just missing. I remember the envelope on the sidewalk, but not that part.
Aside from being knocked down, are you unable to remember any other important part of what happened during the robbery?
No, just that part. I remember the gun and then the envelope on the sidewalk, but getting knocked down is missing—like somebody cut that piece out.
When you saw the gun during the robbery, did you believe that you or someone else might die or be seriously injured?
I’m not sure I thought that clearly at the time. I saw the gun, and it scared me, but I don’t remember believing somebody was going to die or be seriously hurt.
Since the robbery, have there been moments when it felt like you were reliving it, as if it were happening again right then?

Yes. Sometimes I’ll be sitting at my kitchen table and, out of nowhere, I hear that man’s rough voice in my head, or I see the donation envelope hitting the ground. For a moment it feels like I’m right back there.
Since the robbery, have these symptoms been interfering with your day-to-day life?

A little, yes. I haven’t been able to keep up with organizing the Día de los Muertos event the way I usually do. And I’ve stopped going to card nights—I just don’t feel steady around people right now.
When you saw the gun during the robbery, did you think you might be shot?
I—I don’t know. I saw it and I was frightened, but I don’t remember thinking, specifically, that he was going to shoot me.
At the moment you saw the gun, did you believe your life was in danger?
I’m not sure I believed that exactly. I was very scared when I saw it, but I don’t remember thinking, “My life is in danger.”
During the robbery, did you feel helpless?
I’m not sure. I was frightened, but I don’t really remember feeling helpless exactly.
